title: SCIM staged deactivate: operator visibility, rollback, and reconcile UI
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Problem: SCIM deprovision requests from some identity providers sometimes partially complete (user disabled in Redwood but group links remain, or external request times out after downstream success). Operators lack visibility into the in-flight state and cannot safely cancel or roll back automated deprovision. We need an operator-facing workflow: staged deactivate (soft-disable + tombstone metadata), clear operator UI and logs showing the original SCIM operation id and upstream provider, and a reversible rollback path within a configured grace window. This will reduce accidental hard-deletes, shorten incident MTTR, and improve auditability for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Admin console shows a new 'Pending Deactivations' view listing SCIM operations with status (pending, partial, failed, completed). Each row shows SCIM operation id, provider, timestamp, affected user ids, and reason codes.
Operators can cancel a pending deactivation which triggers a rollback attempt: re-enable account, restore group links, and annotate audit logs with rollback outcome.
All SCIM provisioning events (create/update/disable/delete) are enriched with scim_operation_id and upstream_user_id in the audit log; logs are queryable in Console with filters.
A background reconcile job detects mismatches (Redwood active vs provider state) and surfaces candidates in the UI; reconcile run history is recorded as audit events.
Automated tests cover idempotency (replaying same SCIM op leads to no duplicate side effects) and rollback happy/failure paths.
Documentation updated with admin runbook describing the staged deactivate lifecycle and manual recovery steps.
implementation_notes: API: extend internal provisioning API to accept ?staged=true flag and return scim_operation_id for tracking.
DB: add ProvisionEvent table row for each incoming SCIM op with fields (scim_operation_id, provider, raw_payload_reference, status, tombstone_until).

Deprovision flow: 1) mark user as soft_disabled (login blocked), 2) create tombstone with list of removed group links and ACLs, 3) enqueue reconcile job to verify downstream effects and wait for grace_window before hard_delete.
Audit: augment audit events (actor=SCIM-sync) with scim_operation_id and list of side effects; ensure retention policy aligns with compliance (90 days for enriched events).
Console: new 'Pending Deactivations' page + action buttons (Cancel/Force Delete/Send Reconcile). Wire to GraphQL endpoints with RBAC checks (only admins/org-owners).
Reconcile job: incremental idempotent worker that uses scim_operation_id to correlate downstream responses and retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Store last_attempt and failure_reason.
Metrics: track pending_deactivations_count, rollback_attempts, reconcile_failures, mean_time_to_rollback for SLO dashboards.
risk_mitigation: Keep staged deactivation behind a feature flag (org-level) for initial rollout; default rollout to test orgs only.
Limit grace_window default to 7 days and make configurable per-org to reduce exposure.
Add rate limits for manual rollback actions to prevent abusive mass reactivations.
Implement strong idempotency by keying side-effect writes on scim_operation_id to avoid duplicate group attachments on replay.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): feature-flag enabled in staging for core team; run reconcile jobs hourly against shadow SCIM feeds.
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 10 pilot customers and one major IdP integration (Okta); collect operator feedback and metrics.
Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to more orgs, expose console UI, and enable default tombstone retention per org policy.
Phase 4 (GA): flip feature flag on for all orgs and publish admin runbook and audit schema changes.
qa_test_plan: Unit tests for ProvisionEvent creation and tombstone lifecycle transitions.
Integration test: simulate IdP timeout after disabling user; reconcile should detect partial success and mark operation partial; manual rollback restores group links.
E2E: UI test for 'Pending Deactivations' list, cancel button behavior, and audit log queryability.
Chaos test: worker crashes mid-reconcile to validate idempotent retry semantics.
